title: Arts in the Age of Data: skill trees
intro: Four skill trees: the data project, the critical lens on the age of data, the tools and the teamwork. Pick a badge to see its skills, tick what you've learned, and watch the trees light up. Your read-out below turns it into language for CVs, applications and interviews.

stages.label: Set up
stages.blurb: Form the team, pick a topic, plan.

setup.question: Why this topic, and whose story does the data tell?

find.question: Who collected this data, and what does it leave out?

prepare.question: What assumptions are you building in as you clean and combine?

analyse.question: Could something else explain this pattern?

visualise.question: Does your design inform, or does it spin?

tell.question: What do the findings mean, and for whom?

blurbs.excel-l1: Spreadsheet basics: tidy, sort, filter, calculate.
blurbs.tableau-l2: Dashboards, maps and stories in Tableau.
blurbs.data-creator: Build data that doesn't exist yet.
blurbs.adv-data-types: JSON, maps, text and survey weights.
blurbs.launch: Choose a topic and plan the project.
blurbs.tp1: Play your part in the group.
blurbs.tp2: Own your part; give and take feedback.
blurbs.age-context: Where data comes from, and who it serves.
blurbs.analyst: Spot patterns and explain them honestly.
blurbs.data-humanist: Interpret findings with nuance and context.
blurbs.infographic: Plan and lay out an infographic.
blurbs.integrated: Combine writing and charts in one piece.

badges.cv: Designed an infographic with a clear structure, visual hierarchy and flow, planned from a sketched layout.
Produced an integrated report combining concise written analysis with titled, captioned data visualisations for a non-specialist audience.
Developed my data storytelling by recreating landmark visualisations and learning from current work.

badges.blurb: Read the patterns and test your explanations.
badges.cv: Identified patterns in data, framed testable hypotheses and made the assumptions behind my analysis explicit.

badges.label: Chart Repertoire
badges.blurb: More chart types, and when each one fits.
badges.cv: Chose from a wide range of chart types, including tree maps, radar, area and population pyramid charts, to suit the data and the question.
badges.story: Tell me about a time you chose a less familiar chart type. Why was it the right one?
badges.next: Keep a swipe file of chart types you see in the news, with a note on what each is good for.

trees.label: Critical Lens on the Age of Data
trees.sub: One badge per lecture, up to your own essay

badges.label: The Age of Data
badges.cv: Placed my work in the wider context of the age of data and its consequences for society.
badges.story: Why does your project's topic matter now? What has changed because this data exists?
badges.blurb: Week 1: what the age of data is, and what it changes.

badges.label: The Data State
badges.cv: Examined how states have used data to govern, and the trade-off between surveillance and freedom.
badges.story: Tell me about a time you weighed the benefits of collecting data against the risks to privacy.
badges.blurb: Week 2: power, freedom and the birth of the data state.

badges.label: Algorithms and Justice
badges.cv: Evaluated how data and algorithms can encode bias and injustice, and who bears the harm.
badges.story: Give an example of data or an algorithm treating groups unfairly. How would you spot that in your own work?
badges.blurb: Week 3: oppressive algorithms, inequity and justice.

badges.label: Seeing Data
badges.cv: Decoded landmark visualisations to work out the data behind them, and how design can inform or mislead.
badges.story: Pick a famous chart. What data sits behind it, and what did its designer want you to see?
badges.blurb: Week 4: the top 50 data visualisations of all time.

badges.label: Ideology and Metrics
badges.cv: Assessed what common metrics such as GDP capture and leave out, and the values built into them.
badges.story: Tell me about a measure you used in your project. What does it miss, and how did you deal with that?
badges.blurb: Week 5: ideology and metrics.

badges.label: Asking the People
badges.cv: Critically assessed social surveys: who is asked, how questions are worded and why the data was collected.
badges.story: Describe a survey you relied on. How confident were you in it, and why?
badges.blurb: Week 7: social surveys, sex and what you ask.

badges.label: AI and the Data State
badges.cv: Considered how AI depends on data, and who gains and loses from data-driven technologies.
badges.story: How should someone in your future job think about using AI tools on data? What would you check?
badges.blurb: Week 10: AI, capitalism and the future of the data state.

badges.label: Sorting and Classifying
badges.cv: Questioned the categories data uses to sort people, including how poverty and social class are measured.
badges.story: Tell me about a category in your data that didn't fit reality neatly. What did you do?
badges.blurb: Week 8: sorting and classifying, poverty and social class.

badges.label: Polling and Democracy
badges.cv: Interpreted opinion polls critically, judging samples, margins of error and representativeness.
badges.story: A poll says 52% support a policy. What would you want to know before believing it?
badges.blurb: Week 9: politics, polling and who you ask.
The peak: put your own project, and your essay, into the story of the age of data.
badges.cv: Situated my own data project within the history and politics of the age of data, and contributed to its study through an extended essay.
badges.story: How does your project, or your essay, add to our understanding of the age of data?

badges.cv: Used lookup, conditional and summary functions, pivot tables and Power Query to clean, combine and summarise datasets in Excel.
Built interactive Excel outputs with pivot charts, calculated fields, slicers and conditional formatting.

badges.label: Form the Team
badges.blurb: Form a group and agree how you'll work together.
badges.cv: Formed a project team and agreed ways of working, including how we would communicate and make decisions.
badges.story: How did your group agree to work together at the start? What would you do differently next time?

badges.label: Collaborate I
badges.story: Tell me about a time your group disagreed. What did you do, and what was the outcome?
badges.cv: Worked in a group project with a clear role, completing shared tasks.
badges.blurb: Take a role and do your share.

badges.label: Collaborate II
badges.story: Tell me about a time your group disagreed. What did you do, and what was the outcome?
badges.cv: Resolved disagreements by finding compromises, and shared my skills with teammates.
badges.blurb: Find compromises; share what you know.

badges.label: Collaborate III
badges.story: Tell me about a time your group disagreed. What did you do, and what was the outcome?
badges.cv: Supported teammates who were stuck so the whole group could move forward.
badges.blurb: Help a teammate who's stuck.

badges.label: Communicate I
badges.story: How did your group keep track of decisions? What was your part in that?
badges.cv: Recorded group decisions and action points in meetings.
badges.blurb: Write up the action list.

badges.label: Communicate II
badges.story: How did your group keep track of decisions? What was your part in that?
badges.cv: Kept a team informed with regular progress updates and a weekly decision log.
badges.blurb: Keep everyone posted; keep the log.

badges.label: Communicate III
badges.story: How did your group keep track of decisions? What was your part in that?
badges.cv: Chaired group meetings, keeping discussion focused and decisions recorded.
badges.blurb: Chair the meeting.

badges.label: Feedback I
badges.story: Describe feedback you received on your work. What did you change because of it?
badges.cv: Sought feedback on my work from teammates.
badges.blurb: Ask for feedback.

badges.label: Feedback II
badges.story: Describe feedback you received on your work. What did you change because of it?
badges.cv: Gave specific, constructive feedback to teammates.
badges.blurb: Give useful feedback.

badges.label: Feedback III
badges.story: Describe feedback you received on your work. What did you change because of it?
badges.cv: Acted on feedback to improve my work, and explained what changed.
badges.blurb: Act on it.

badges.label: Deliver I
badges.story: Tell me about a deadline that was hard to meet. How did you make sure your part was delivered?
badges.cv: Took ownership of a distinct part of a group project, agreeing my individual focus.
badges.blurb: Own your part of the project.

badges.label: Deliver II
badges.story: Tell me about a deadline that was hard to meet. How did you make sure your part was delivered?
badges.cv: Delivered agreed actions to deadline as part of a team.
badges.blurb: Hit agreed targets and deadlines.

badges.label: Deliver III
badges.story: Tell me about a deadline that was hard to meet. How did you make sure your part was delivered?
badges.cv: Brought a group's work together into a finished final submission.
badges.blurb: Bring the final piece together.

badges.label: Lead I
badges.story: Tell me about a time a project went off track. How did you notice, and what did you do?
badges.cv: Monitored a team's progress against its plan, consulting colleagues on the way forward.
badges.blurb: Check the team's on track.

badges.label: Lead II
badges.story: Tell me about a time a project went off track. How did you notice, and what did you do?
badges.cv: Built agreement within a team on key decisions.
badges.blurb: Build agreement.

badges.label: Lead III
badges.story: Tell me about a time a project went off track. How did you notice, and what did you do?
badges.cv: Led a team's response when a project went off track, including at a formal progress review.
badges.blurb: Steer the group through trouble.

lens-consequences.label: Weigh the consequences of datafication
lens-consequences.desc: Think through what turning life into data changes for people and society.

lens-surveillance.label: Surveillance and freedom
lens-surveillance.desc: Ask what data collection costs in privacy and freedom, and who decides.

lens-bias.label: Bias in data and algorithms
lens-bias.desc: Spot how bias gets built into data and automated decisions.

lens-harm.label: Who is harmed, who benefits?
lens-harm.desc: Ask who gains and who loses when decisions are made by data.

lens-decode.label: Decode a visualisation
lens-decode.desc: Work out the data behind a chart and how it was combined.

lens-metric-limits.label: What a metric leaves out
lens-metric-limits.desc: Say what a measure such as GDP captures and what it misses.

lens-wording.label: How you ask shapes the answer
lens-wording.desc: Notice how question wording and order affect survey results.

lens-categories.label: Question the categories
lens-categories.desc: Ask who designed the categories data sorts people into, and why.

lens-class.label: Measuring poverty and class
lens-class.desc: Understand how poverty and social class have been defined and counted.

lens-sample.label: Who was asked?
lens-sample.desc: Judge whether a poll's sample represents the people it claims to.

lens-ai-data.label: What did the AI learn from?
lens-ai-data.desc: Ask what data an AI system was trained on, and what that means for its outputs.

lens-ai-power.label: AI, capital and power
lens-ai-power.desc: Weigh who gains from AI and the data economy.

team-share-skills.label: Share a skill
team-share-skills.desc: Teach a teammate something you know how to do.

team-decision-log.label: Keep the decision log
team-decision-log.desc: Record decisions and named contributions in the weekly log.

team-chair.label: Chair a meeting
team-chair.desc: Run a group meeting so it ends with clear decisions and actions.

team-act-feedback.label: Act on feedback
team-act-feedback.desc: Change your work in response to feedback, and say what changed.

team-deadline.label: Meet a group deadline
team-deadline.desc: Get your part done in time for the rest of the group.

team-final.label: Bring it together
team-final.desc: Combine the group's work into the final submission.

team-midpoint.label: Lead the mid-point review
team-midpoint.desc: Speak for the group at the review with staff.

viz-sketch.label: Sketch the layout first
viz-sketch.desc: Plan the page on paper before you build it.

viz-hierarchy.label: Lead with the key message
viz-hierarchy.desc: Give the most important finding the most visual weight.

report-captions.label: Title and caption every chart
report-captions.desc: Give each chart a title that says what it shows, and a source line.

lens-define.label: Define the age of data
lens-define.desc: Explain what is meant by the age of data, and when and why it began.

lens-essay.label: Write about the age of data
lens-essay.desc: Contribute to the study of the age of data in an essay of your own.

hero.label: All Round Data Hero
hero.blurb: Every badge in all four trees.
